elements.problem: Header maps to an Urgent priority evaluation anchored on Mental disorder with an (or ...) of the listed outcomes, per house pattern. Urgent level matches 'urgent attention'/'refer urgently'. Whether the outcomes list is complete is judged on the individual bullets.
evidence: Urgent: mentally ill patient at risk of harm or property damage if referral delayed :: Urgent (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Mental disorder" "disorder")) (or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "At increased risk of self-injurious behavior" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "At increased risk for suicide" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "High risk of harm to others" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "At increased risk for destructive behavior to property" "finding"))))
Check for urgent risks in the mentally ill patient needing admission :: due_to (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Mental disorder" "disorder"))

parts_missing: Risk of death from the mental illness (e.g. self-neglect, refusal to eat/drink, catatonia) as a separate trigger
elements.problem: No check_for item or priority criterion for death. Suicide covers only one route to death; death from self-neglect or medical consequences of the illness is not captured. Closest available SNOMED: 'High risk of self neglect' / 'At increased risk for self neglect' (finding), neither used.

elements.scope_reason: 'Irreversible health problem/s' is vague; there is no precise SNOMED concept, but a proxy (e.g. 'At increased risk for self neglect') exists and the builder could at least have flagged it.
parts_missing: Irreversible health problems due to delayed referral
elements.problem: Not encoded in check_for or the priority rule, and no proxy concept used.

Split into harm to self (self-injurious behaviour risk + suicide risk) and harm to others; all are checked for and used in the priority (or). 'High risk of harm to self' does not exist in SNOMED, so the self-injury/suicide pair is a reasonable substitute. Minor point: the page says 'serious' harm; the self-injury concept is 'increased risk' rather than 'high risk'.

parts_missing: 'loss of property' (e.g. giving away or squandering possessions/money in mania) is not covered by a destructive-behaviour concept
elements.problem: 'At increased risk for destructive behavior to property' covers damage to property but not loss of property.

elements.problem: Its urgency is reflected in the Urgent priority level.

elements.scope_reason: Mostly management (restraint, MHCA 48) plus a cross-reference to p35. 'Aggressive/disruptive' is a finding (Aggressive behavior is a warning sign) that the page attaches to this patient in the urgent box, but as a management trigger, not an urgency criterion.
parts_missing: Aggressive/disruptive behaviour is not checked for or linked
elements.problem: Aggression appears nowhere in the rules. It is defensible because it is a warning sign handled on p35, but a mentally ill patient who is aggressive is the commonest real case of 'harm to others'. The rules depend on the user recording a risk-assessment finding instead.
Routes to p36 (confusion/delirium). Altered consciousness is handled there.
Capacity to consent decides the legal admission status (MHCA), not triage or diagnosis.
Branches on refusal decide the legal status.

The criteria for involuntary admission (harm to self/others, serious damage to financial interests/reputation) decide the legal pathway in the non-emergency branch, not urgency. The 'financial interests/reputation' criterion has no SNOMED encoding and is legal, not clinical.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: mentally ill patient at risk of harm or property damage if referral delayed
rule_level_problems.problem: The (or ...) covers only 2 of the 4 red-box outcomes (harm to self/others, property). The 'Death' and 'Irreversible health problem/s' bullets have no criterion, so a mentally ill patient at risk of dying from self-neglect, or not eating or drinking, without suicidal intent, gets no Urgent flag.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: mentally ill patient at risk of harm or property damage if referral delayed
rule_level_problems.problem: The page's criterion is conditional ('if a delay in referral may lead to ...'). The rules approximate it with present risk findings, a reasonable modelling choice that should be noted.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent risks in the mentally ill patient needing admission
rule_level_problems.problem: The trigger is (clinical_finding 'Mental disorder'). It fires only when a mental disorder (or a descendant) is recorded as a finding. There is no link to the aggression warning sign or to suicidal ideation as entry points. Fine under the house standard, but worth noting for the anchoring.

summary: The most consequential gap: the red-box outcomes 'Death' and 'Irreversible health problem/s' are not encoded, so the Urgent rule fires only on self-harm, suicide, harm-to-others or property-damage risk; a 'self neglect' risk concept was available as a proxy. 'Loss of property' is only partly covered by the destructive-behaviour concept. Otherwise the check list and priority rule agree, all concepts exist, and the flowchart on the rest of the page is legal-status routing and rightly out of scope.
